newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SMITH ORDERS WALLABIES TO SHOW AGGRESSION.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMITH ORDERS WALLABIES TO SHOW AGGRESSION.

text.p: Australia coach Greg Smith ordered his players to show more aggression after making six changes on Tuesday for the one-off rugby union test against England on Saturday.
Smith, disgusted by his side's performance in their 30-13 defeat by New Zealand in Christchurch last Saturday, criticised the forwards, with the front row bearing the brunt of his anger.
Prop Richard Harry, hooker Marco Caputo and lock Matt Cockbain were among those dropped in reaction to the All Blacks' overwhelming dominance in the scrum at Lancaster Park.
Earlier, Smith delivered a stern lecture to his players about their lack of spirit and determination against the All Blacks.
Speaking after the team meeting, Smith said: "I don't believe we did justice to ourselves. I wanted them to know that we (the Wallaby team selectors) were disgusted with what happened."

Domestic news agency Australian Associated Press said Smith launched into a tirade during the meeting, telling the players they must assert themselves physically against England, even if it meant taking matters into their own hands.
Smith said he would prefer them to fight back rather than lie down and allow the opposition to commit professional fouls and interference with impunity, the report said.
Asked by Reuters to comment on the report, Smith angrily declined to confirm or deny making the statements in what he insisted was an emotional, but private, team meeting.

Uncapped prop Cameron Blades, hooker Michael Foley and lock Garrick Morgan have been drafted into the side by Smith to add scrummaging power for the clash at the Sydney Football Stadium against the Triple Crown winners.
Australia may make one further change in the forwards after naming four players -- Troy Coker, Daniel Manu, Brett Robinson and David Wilson -- for the back row.
Coker played at number eight with Robinson and Wilson as flankers against the All Blacks but Smith said he would make a final decision later in the week.
"Australia have to have a scrum that does not lose. Our front row was not as effective as we wanted it to be (against New Zealand) on Saturday," Smith told reporters.
In the backs, full-back Matthew Burke and centre Jason Little return from injury at the expense of Stephen Larkham and Daniel Herbert.
Centre James Holbeck was named in the starting line-up as a replacement for Pat Howard, who fractured his ankle and damaged ligaments in an awkward fall in a tackle against New Zealand.

Australia (from): Matthew Burke, Joe Roff, Jason Little, James Holbeck, Ben Tune, Tim Horan, George Gregan, Troy Coker, Daniel Manu, Brett Robinson, David Wilson, John Eales (captain), Garrick Morgan, Cameron Blades, Michael Foley, Ewen McKenzie.
(Note: one of Coker, Manu, Robinson or Wilson to be omitted).
